messages:
Aisha: Hey folks — quick relocation Q. I'm moving from CA -> OR in ~3 weeks. Two quick ones: 1) Will my monthly WFH stipend continue? 2) Anything I need to do for payroll / benefits / taxes so my pay doesn't get messed up? Thanks!

Eden: Congrats on the move! Short answers: WFH stipend continues for US domestic moves (no action needed on our end besides updating your work location). For international moves it's case-by-case and requires manager + People Ops approval.

Eden: A couple of important notes: the stipend is taxable income and payroll withholding is tied to your payroll address. So we need you to update your home address in Workday/payroll before your move date so state withholding is correct.

Jon: Quick Q — OR has no personal income tax, right? Do you still need to change state withholding when moving from CA -> OR?

Maya: OR does have income tax (it does). WA is the state with no income tax. Regardless: any state change requires us to update withholding and unemployment filings. Please fill the location-change form so payroll can switch your state tax profile and benefits zip codes.

Aisha: Got it. Is stipend pro-rated if I move mid-month?

Eden: Yes — stipend is pro-rated for the month of the move. Payroll will calculate a pro-rated payment for that pay period.

hr-bot: Reminder: Please submit the Location Change Form at least 7 business days before your move to avoid withholding delays. Link: <internal:location-change-form>

Aisha: Any chance this single move triggers a tax nexus for Redwood (like requiring the company to register in OR)?

Maya: Very unlikely for one employee. Nexus thresholds are usually based on payroll headcount, revenue, or physical presence beyond a small headcount. If multiple employees relocate to the same state or we start placing equipment/servers there then legal/finance will evaluate registration. We'll proactively review if we see more moves into OR.

Jon: For contractors who move states, is it the same flow?

Eden: Contractors are different. We don't manage their benefits; they need to update their contractor forms/1099 info and coordinate with their vendor manager. Any cross-border contracting may require contract amendments and legal review.

Maya: Practical next steps for you @Aisha: 1) Fill Location Change Form: <internal:location-change-form> 2) Upload proof of new address (lease or utility bill) if requested 3) Confirm benefits zip-code (health plan eligibility can change by zip) 4) Payroll will apply pro-rated stipend and adjust withholding

Eden: I'll monitor the form and confirm once payroll completes the change. If any benefits eligibility changes (e.g., provider network), we'll loop you in.

Aisha: Awesome — thanks. One last: can I keep home-office stipend while I look for housing for a short gap (2 weeks between leases)?

Eden: Short gaps are fine as long as your primary residence is updated in the system within 30 days. For gaps >30 days, we need manager + People Ops approval. Stipend continues while you remain an active employee and your location is in an eligible country.

Maya: If you want to see the fields we'll ask for, here's the minimal form snippet we use: ``` Location Change Form - minimal fields - employee_name - employee_id - current_state - new_state - effective_move_date (YYYY-MM-DD) - new_address_zip - proof_of_address_attachment - manager_approval (yes/no) - notes ```

Eden: Thanks all. @Maya please flag if payroll sees other inbound OR moves this quarter. Aisha — ping me once you submit the form and I'll confirm stipend pro-ration.

Maya: Will do :thumbsup:

Aisha: Submitted the form just now. Thanks everyone! :wave:
